name: Nearly-Sorted Object-Space Visibility Ordering
definition: A relaxation of exact sorting where fragments are allowed to be up to k positions out of order in object-space, allowing for faster sorting algorithms while requiring exact sorting during fragment processing.
summary: Nearly-Sorted Object-Space Visibility Ordering uses approximate object-space sorting to produce fragments within a bounded error, enabling faster processing than exact per-pixel sorting while deferring final correctness to a linear-time fragment correction step.
